title: One Photo, One Comment, In The Log
objective: Photograph one finished piece of your own work on the log frame, then write one comment that names the step you took and one thing you would change.

blocks.text: BUILD · Art · Week 5. Trinity Arts Award Discover. One Photo, One Comment, In The Log.
Objective: photograph one finished piece of your own work on the log frame, then write one comment that names the step you took and one thing you would change.
Success evidence: one clear photo in the log box, one comment in your own words, and today's date.
You photograph your own work and nothing else. You do not photograph a person. No faces, no names, no rooms at home. The piece on the desk is the whole shot.
40 minutes. Offline.

stages.title: Arrival · retrieve
stages.data-ta1: Log sheets and the grey card out before pupils sit down. One camera per table, face down until the I Do.
stages.data-ta2: If a pupil turns the camera on a person, or starts talking about home, put their piece back on the card and name it. Do not comment.

blocks.text: A log is proof that you did it
Your arts log holds what you made this term.
Each page holds two things. A photo, and a comment.
The photo shows the work. The comment says what you did to it.
One without the other is half a page.
A photo with no words tells nobody what you chose.
A comment with no photo shows nobody the work.
Read the two-part rule once and leave it on the board. Every pupil should be able to say photo and comment before the starter runs.
You need three things today. Your finished piece, the log sheet, and the grey card.
Three words matter today. Frame. Glare. Comment.
The frame is the part the photo holds.
Glare is white shine sitting on top of your work.
The comment is the line you write under the photo.
You will use all three words before you leave.

stages.title: Starter · create the need
stages.data-ta1: Hold the two photos up side by side. Do not say which one is better; let them find it.

blocks.text: Two photos of one piece
Here are two photos. Both show the same drawing.
In photo one the drawing fills the frame. You can see every mark on it.
In photo two the drawing sits far away. A pencil case sits next to it.
Both photos are real photos. Only one of them is evidence.
Evidence means an adult can see what you did.
Nobody has written a word yet. The frame did all the work.

items: 1 · fill the frame with the work.
2 · take the other stuff out of the shot.
3 · check that the marks still show.

blocks.text: Now look for glare on photo two.
There is a white patch across the top of the paper.
That patch hides a mark you spent ten minutes on.
A photo cannot prove a mark that nobody can see.

stages.title: I Do · model
stages.data-ta1: Model one piece only. Take the poor shot first, then fix it in front of the group.

blocks.text: Four steps to a log photo
Watch me log one piece. I use four steps every time.
First I place my piece flat on the grey card.
The card is plain, so the edge of my work shows.
Second I turn the card to face the window.
Light from the side leaves a shadow across the page.
Light from the front does not. Turn the card, not the light.
Third I hold the camera straight over the work.
Straight on keeps the shape true. A slant makes a square look bent.
I move in close until the work fills the frame.

boxes.head: PLACE
boxes.line1: work flat on the grey card

boxes.head: LIGHT
boxes.line1: turn it to face the window

blocks.caption: Four steps in this order, every time you log a piece
blocks.title: From finished piece to log photo
blocks.alt: Four boxes joined by arrows: place the work down, turn it to the light, shoot straight on, then check the picture

blocks.text: Fourth I look at the photo, not at the work.
I check three things. The marks, the glare, and the edges.
My first shot has glare on it. So I turn the card and shoot again.
Say each step name out loud as you do it. Place, light, shoot, check. The four words are the thing being taught, not the photograph.
One shot is rarely the right shot. Two or three shots is normal.
If two shots both fail, move the card and not the camera.
Keep the best shot. Delete the rest before you sit down.

stages.title: We Do · everyone commits
stages.data-ta1: Six photo cards and four fault cards on each table. Nobody speaks until every table has two piles.

blocks.text: Sort the photo cards, then match the faults
There are six photo cards on your table.
Sort them into two piles. Log ready, and not ready yet.
Now take the pile that is not ready.
Match each card to one fault card. Glare, blur, too far, or a person in the shot.
Every card gets a fault, even when you are not sure.
A guess I can see beats a card left face down.
Then hold up the one card your table argued about.
Two tables may match the same card in two ways.
Both tables give one reason. We do not vote on it.

stages.title: I Do 2 · connect
stages.data-ta1: Comment frame face up beside the log sheet. The comment is built from the frame, never from memory.

blocks.text: The comment that goes under the photo
Now for the words. One comment goes under each photo.
A good comment names the step you took.
Then it names one thing you would change next time.
Here is my comment. I drew the key with a hard mark.
Next time I would press more lightly at the top.
That tells an adult two things. What I did, and what I saw.

boxes.head: NAMES THE STEP
boxes.line1: says what you did to it

blocks.caption: The same photo sits under both; only one of them earns the page
blocks.title: A comment that works and one that fails
blocks.alt: Two boxes side by side: one comment naming the step taken, one comment saying only that the work was good

blocks.text: Nice is not a comment. Good is not a comment.
Those words tell nobody what you actually did.
Use the frame printed on your sheet. It gives you two lines.
Line one starts with the words: I made this by.
Line two starts with the words: next time I would.
Fill both lines and your comment is finished.

items: 1 · name the tool or the mark you used.
2 · name the step you took with it.
3 · name one change for next time.
4 · read it back and check that it is true.

blocks.text: Keep the comment short. Two true lines beat six vague ones.

stages.title: We Do 2 · lab
stages.data-ta1: Pair pupils by table, not by choice. Two minutes each way, timed out loud.
stages.data-ta2: Cameras point down at the desk between shots. A shot of a face is deleted at once, without a discussion.

blocks.text: Check a partner's photo
Work in twos. You swap sheets, never cameras.
Look at your partner's photo for ten seconds.
Then say one fault word. Glare, blur, too far, or clear.
Clear means the photo is ready for the log.
Point at the part of the photo you mean.
Your partner takes one more shot if they need it.
You may not say that it is fine.
Fine gives the other person nothing to change.
Then swap back and check your own photo the same way.
You are allowed to keep a photo your partner faulted.
Say why you kept it. That reason goes on the sheet.

stages.title: Independent · evidence
stages.data-ta1: Scribe the exact words only. Do not tidy a rough comment into a better one.
stages.data-ta2: A pupil who will not write may say the comment aloud. Record it word for word and note that it was spoken.

blocks.text: One photo, one comment, one date
Work on your own now.
Take your photo using the four steps.
Place, light, shoot, check. Say them under your breath.
Then put the photo in the box on your log sheet.
Write your comment on the two lines under it.
Write today's date in the corner of the sheet.
A log page with no date proves nothing later.

items: Supported · take the photo and write line one of the frame.
Standard · take the photo, write both lines, and add the date.
Stretch · as Standard, and name which of the four steps you had to fix.

blocks.text: Log a piece that you made yourself.
Do not log work that belongs to somebody else.
If you finish early, take one more photo up close.
A close photo shows a small mark that the wide one lost.
Put the close photo beside the first one, not over it.

stages.title: Exit · Audience and Influence
stages.data-ta1: The named adult reads the comment back word for word. No paraphrase, however rough it sounds.

blocks.text: Read your comment to one adult
Read your comment to the adult at your table.
They read it back to you exactly as you wrote it.
If that is not what you meant, say it again.
They write the new line underneath the old one.
Then pick the one thing that happens next.
Keep this photo, retake it, or add a second line.
Write your choice on the sheet before you go.
The sheet goes in the arts log folder, not in your bag.
Next week you open the folder before you start.

print.intro: Log the piece you finished today; leave the box empty rather than filling it with a photo nobody can read.
focusRows: One photo, filling the frame, with no glare over the marks
A comment naming the step taken and one change for next time
Today's date written in the corner of the log sheet
tiers: Take the photo using the four steps and write the first line of the comment frame.
Take the photo, write both lines of the comment frame, and add today's date.
As Standard, and name which of the four steps you had to fix to get the shot.
checks: The photo shows the pupil's own finished piece and no person.
The work fills the frame and the marks can still be seen.
The comment names a step taken and one change for next time.
The log sheet carries today's date in the pupil's own hand.
